source: GitHub (euan-forrester/save-file-converter issue #297, 'Add ability to convert MiSTer N64 files'); the same five files are the converter's test data (frontend/tests/data/save-formats/mister/n64)
author: Unknown MiSTer user; attached as 'Example files: MiSTer N64 saves.zip' by euan-forrester (save-file-converter's author) on 2024-04-24. The zip's macOS quarantine records say he downloaded them with Firefox on 2024-04-23.
licence: none stated (a file attached to a public GitHub issue; the repository is GPL-3.0)
what_it_is: A Controller Pak image (port 1) holding five 2-page notes named TWINE: four with game code NO7P (A-D, the PAL release) and one NO7E (A, the US release). 32768 bytes, file dated 2023-12-20 08:00. Not booted here.
note: Attributed to the MiSTer N64 core by the issue ('The new core has all the different possible file types split up') and by the names: '<ROM stem>.eep/.sra/.fla' and '<ROM stem>_1.cpk' are what MiSTer's Main (support/n64/n64.cpp) names N64 saves, and '_N.cpk' is MiSTer's alone. The file dates (Dec 2023 - Feb 2024) are after Main's December 2023 change that split the old single .sav into one file per chip and pak. Main of that time created new save files filled with 0x00 (0xFF since Main commit bc49794, 2026-01-13). Console byte order (a plain .mpk): MiSTer's Main swaps pak data on the way to and from the core. Its ID area is the classic mupen64plus-core template (serial ffffffff 051a5f13..., checksum 6625 99cd), not the header MiSTer's Main used for new paks at the time (serial 0007 0000 0007 c21e...), so the pak was formatted elsewhere and brought to the MiSTer; MiSTer wrote it back whole. The NO7P notes suggest the PAL game was also used with it.
